classification.label: High turbidity / suspended sediment signature

evidence.name: broadband_vis_enhancement
evidence.description: Mean enhancement at 560 and 665 nm relative to background water.

evidence.name: visible_tilt_665_over_443
evidence.description: Enhancement at 665 nm minus enhancement at 443 nm. Mineral particles scatter more efficiently toward the red, so sediment raises red more than blue; dissolved organic matter absorbs blue and does the opposite.

evidence.name: blue_depression_443
evidence.description: Blue reflectance suppressed relative to green without a red-edge peak, the signature of dissolved organic absorption.

evidence.name: phycocyanin_absorption_620
evidence.description: Excess depth of the 620 nm feature over background water. Phycocyanin is a cyanobacterial accessory pigment. This requires narrow bands: Sentinel-2 has no band at 620 nm at all, so a multispectral sensor cannot form this evidence.

evidence.name: red_edge_ratio_705_665
evidence.description: Ratio of the 705 nm enhancement to the 665 nm enhancement. Algal biomass produces a reflectance peak near 700-710 nm that mineral sediment does not.

evidence.name: floating_algae_index
evidence.description: NIR reflectance above the red-to-SWIR baseline (Hu 2009). Positive values indicate material at or above the surface.

evidence.name: chl_absorption_depth_675
evidence.description: Excess depth of the 675 nm chlorophyll-a absorption feature over the local background water, measured against a 650/715 nm continuum. Positive means more pigment absorption than normal here.

caveats: Pixel is 90 m from shore. Bottom reflectance is a competing explanation that a single scene cannot exclude; the temporal baseline test is required.
classification.disclaimer: Optical hypothesis from satellite reflectance. NOT a chemical, biological or toxicological identification. Field sampling and laboratory analysis are required to confirm any interpretation.

params.threshold_rule: empirical percentile of background RX distribution
params.chi2_assumption_note: Chi-squared threshold reported for reference only; the background is a mixture and is not multivariate normal, so the empirical threshold is used.

spec.name: NDWI
spec.interpretation: > 0 generally open water; sensitive to built surfaces
assumptions: Breaks down over bright urban surfaces (use MNDWI there)

spec.name: MNDWI
spec.interpretation: > 0 water; suppresses built-up false positives better than NDWI
assumptions: SWIR is strongly absorbed by water, so contrast is high

spec.name: NDCI
spec.reference: Mishra & Mishra (2012), Remote Sensing of Environment 117:394-406
spec.interpretation: Higher values indicate stronger chlorophyll-a absorption contrast; a screening proxy only
assumptions: Designed for turbid productive inland/coastal water
Loses sensitivity in clear oligotrophic water where the 705 nm peak is weak
Requires an in-situ calibration to become a concentration

spec.name: TURBIDITY_PROXY
spec.reference: Used as the turbidity proxy in the official 813 challenge notebook 06; consistent in form with red-band turbidity indicators such as Nechad et al. (2009), RSE 113:2141-2154
spec.interpretation: Higher values indicate relatively stronger red backscatter, typical of suspended sediment
assumptions: Sensitive to bottom reflectance in shallow water

spec.name: FAI
spec.interpretation: Positive values indicate NIR elevation above the baseline, characteristic of floating/surface algal material
assumptions: More robust to thin cloud and glint than NDVI over water
Detects FLOATING material; subsurface blooms may not register

informative_bands.selection_rule: SNR >= 3 from the product's own uncertainty layer, and 400-900 nm where water-leaving signal exists

metadata.method: Wind-driven surface drift with random-walk diffusion
metadata.wind_source: ERA5 reanalysis via Open-Meteo historical archive API
references: Breivik et al. (2011) wind-induced drift of objects at sea
metadata.coastline_handling: Particles driven onto land are beached at their last water position and stop drifting. beached_fraction reports how much of the cloud has stranded by each horizon.
not_included: Particle settling, resuspension and biological growth or decay
metadata.interpretation: A scenario estimate of where surface material would go under the observed wind alone. Treat the envelope as a search area for field teams, not as a prediction of concentration at a location.
metadata.validation_status: Not validated against observed plume motion for this AOI: no repeat hyperspectral pass and no drifter data were available. Reported as an unvalidated scenario estimate.

wind_sample_point.why: Sampled over offshore water, not at the event centroid, because ERA5's ~25 km grid would otherwise return a land cell.

asset.name: Annaba Port power station
asset.notes: A 72 MW thermal power station on the harbour. Thermal plants draw large volumes of seawater for condenser cooling, so suspended sediment and biofouling load in the source water directly affect screen and heat-exchanger performance. Placed at the mapped plant centroid, not at an intake structure.
asset.why_it_matters: Process water quality and filtration load.

basis: Current separation 0.93 km, asset lies NW of the event centroid.
22.0% of drift particles come within 599 m of the asset by +6 h.
Exposure = proximity 0.922 x trajectory 1.00 x asset sensitivity 0.80 = 0.738.

asset.name: Annaba fishing harbour
asset.notes: Working fishing harbour on the Annaba waterfront. Harbour water quality is both an operational and a compliance concern, and harbours are chronic turbidity sources in their own right.

asset_register.name: Gulf of Annaba operator asset register
asset_register.note: Every asset here is a REAL, publicly mapped coastal feature inside the AOI, with its OpenStreetMap element id recorded so any coordinate can be checked. No coordinate in this file was estimated, and no confidential infrastructure location is included.
asset_register.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, queried via the Overpass API on 2026-09-17 for the AOI bounding box 36.8739,7.5175,37.0599,7.8093
asset_register.licence: OpenStreetMap data is available under the Open Database License (ODbL). (c) OpenStreetMap contributors.
asset_register.policy: BLUEBAN 813 ships no infrastructure database. This register exists so the Gulf of Annaba demonstration runs against real places rather than invented ones. An operator replaces it with their own assets.
asset_register.caveat: A facility asset is placed at the mapped centroid of the facility, which is not the location of its water intake structure. Distances are therefore facility distances, not intake distances.

samples.role_question: What is actually present at the point of strongest signal?
samples.rationale: Highest spectral anomaly in the event (RX 43707). The strongest signal gives laboratory analysis the best chance of identifying what is actually present.

samples.role_question: Has anything reached the protected asset yet?
samples.rationale: Nearest analysable water to Annaba Port power station, 378 m away. This is the measurement that answers whether the asset is affected yet.
expected_variables: Algal toxins if a bloom is suspected

samples.role_question: Where is the boundary, and is the event advancing?
samples.rationale: Edge of the event nearest the modelled drift direction (bearing 273deg). Sampling here tests whether the event is advancing and how sharp the front is.

samples.role_question: What does unaffected water in this body read today?
samples.rationale: Lowest-anomaly water at least 800 m offshore (RX 1.2). Without a same-day control, an absolute laboratory value from the event cannot be interpreted.
expected_variables: Same analyte suite as the event core, for direct comparison

samples.role_question: Where is the interpretation least certain?
samples.rationale: Marginal anomaly (RX between the 85th and 97th percentile) in shallow water, where bottom reflectance and suspended matter are hard to separate optically. A depth reading and a TSS sample here would resolve the ambiguity for the whole nearshore band.
